claims.text: Failure modes / security (input validated at the boundary): a malformed evidence record (metrics or monthly summary not a list of objects, vat_stagger not 1/2/3, ruleset not an object with a text id, statement not an object, malformed accounts/buckets) is refused with exit 2 naming the field, never raised as a traceback or reported as a mismatch (exit 1). Before this change 4 such shapes raised AttributeError/ValueError with exit 1.

Idempotency / partial failure: verify is read-only; verifying a signed pack twice leaves every file in the case folder byte-identical (no lock, log or pack file written), so it can be re-run any number of times.
P13 and P3 invariant tests and the R44/R45/v0 contract tests pass, including refusal of another ruleset naming package version, ruleset id and sha256.

notes: Gaps for the owner: (1) Observability: no log line or alert for verify; it is an offline CLI whose exit codes (0 ok, 1 mismatch, 2 refused) are its signal. A structured case-log/report line is out of this task's scope. (2) Docs: README.md does not mention `cma verify` or its exit codes; there is no changelog line yet. (3) verify sets os.environ[CMA_RULESET] for the duration of a call, which is process-global. That is fine for the CLI, but a multi-threaded caller (MCP, workspace) would need the ruleset passed as a parameter, which is a design change. (4) Authz: verify reads any file the OS user can read (the statement path in the record), but only uses it if its sha256 matches the recorded hash. No new privilege is involved; access is the case root's owner-only permissions (R31). (5) `ruff check .` reports findings only in .bridgie/runs leftovers inside the worktree, not in project code; `ruff check src tests evals` is clean.
